2. A pass that loses yards (a dump) is free.
3. The pass after a dump must be caught in a different lane from the one the dump was thrown from. If it isn't, play goes on but the Jedi point can't be scored on that possession.

**Scoring**

A goal scores 2. A "Jedi" scores 1 straight away: a dump, then a pass into another lane that is caught upfield of where the dump was thrown from. The defence scores 1 for a turnover in the lane the disc was dumped from. Play to 9.

**What the rules push players to do**

Going backwards only pays if the disc then goes somewhere new. Handlers look for the swing as the dump is in the air, and cutters learn to attack the lane the swing is heading for.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Stall 6, even numbers, and the Jedi only scores if the swing is caught upfield of the original thrower.
- 2s: Stall 8, 7v6 or 5v4. Any dump followed by a pass into another lane scores the point, so the dump and swing itself is rewarded.

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "After the dump, where was the space?"
- Ask: "Who moved first to make the swing possible?"
- Ask: "When did a reset gain yards, and what made that happen?"
- Ask: "After the dump, where was the space? Who moved first to make the swing possible?"

**Harder**

- Stall 5; two Jedis needed before a goal counts.

**Easier**

- A spare attacker; two lanes instead of three.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 36.
drills.setup_instructions: A full-width pitch about 40 m long with endzones. Cone lines split it lengthways into three lanes: left, middle and right. 7v7, or 5v5 on a narrower pitch.

drills.title: Double-team trap game
drills.description:
A sideline trap made worse than any real one, so that squaring up and resetting early become the obvious answer.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Normal ultimate at stall 8.
2. When the disc is in a trap zone, a second defender may join the mark until stall 6, then must leave.
3. Walk the square-up and the two-player handler reset through once before playing.

**Scoring**

A goal scores 1. A goal from a possession that got out of a double team within two passes scores 2. A stall or a turnover in a trap zone scores 1 for the defence.

**What the rules push players to do**

With two markers on the disc, someone is free. Throwers learn to square up to the middle and find them; the reset and cutters learn to attack the break side and the middle rather than the line.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Joint session game. With stronger groups the double team may stay until stall 8.
- 2s: With newer groups the second defender leaves at stall 4, or the offence plays 5v4.

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "With two markers on you, where was the space?"
- Ask: "Who was left free, and how did they show you?"
- Ask: "What did the team gain by getting off the line in two passes?"
- Ask: "With two markers on you, where was the space? Who was left free?"

**Harder**

- The double team stays until stall 8.

**Easier**

- The second defender leaves at stall 4.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 21.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v5 on a 30 x 20 m pitch with endzones. A cone line 3 m inside each sideline marks the trap zones.
drills.source: Plan; HN Handler Situations; HN Excel Premium

drills.title: Deep-shot game
drills.description:
A long, narrow pitch that gives deep cutters room and makes the huck to an isolated cutter the best play.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Normal ultimate with a one-way force.
2. Any throw may score, but the pitch is too narrow for lazy swings.

**Scoring**

A goal from a huck over 30 m caught in stride scores 3. Any other goal scores 1.

**What the rules push players to do**

Throwers look long when a cutter is isolated and hold the disc when they aren't. Deep cutters wait for power position, start shallow and commit.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: 5v5, and from week 45 the huck must go to the break side to score 3.
- 2s: 5v4, and a huck over 25 m scores 3.

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "When was the deep shot on? What told you?"
- Ask: "What set the huck up: a swing, a dish, or power position?"
- Ask: "Deep cutters: when did you start, and what were you watching?"

**Harder**

- The huck must be thrown to the break side.

**Easier**

- A spare attacker; a shorter huck counts.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 28.
drills.setup_instructions: A pitch the full length but half the width, with endzones. 5v5 (1s) or 5v4 (2s).
drills.source: Plan; after Ian French, long- and short-throw bonus points

drills.title: Mark-call game
drills.description:
Switching between the triangle mark and the flat mark on a sideline call, under real throws.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Normal ultimate, starting in the triangle mark.
2. Once in each possession the defending team's caller shouts "triangle" or "flat". The mark must change at once and downfield defenders adjust to the new open side.
3. In the harder round the call can come twice.

**Scoring**

A goal scores 1. The defence scores 1 if the mark has changed within a second of the call, and 1 for a stall or a block.

**What the rules push players to do**

The mark practises the switch while a thrower is trying to break it, and the sideline practises calling early enough to be useful.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' game in week 9.
- 2s: The 2s don't need the flat mark yet. Their version is the tram-line game with sideline calls.

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "What did the thrower get in the second before you changed?"
- Ask: "Downfield: how did you know the open side had moved?"

**Harder**

- The call comes at stall 4, or twice in a possession.

**Easier**

- The call comes before the first throw.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 9.
drills.setup_instructions: 4v4 (then 5v5) on a 30 x 20 m pitch. One caller per team on the sideline.

drills.title: Back-shoulder game
drills.description:
The 2s' version of Space Invaders: one priority only, deep first.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Normal ultimate at stall 8.
2. Defenders start every cut on the cutter's deep, open-side shoulder.

**Scoring**

An under caught costs the defence nothing. A deep catch (past the defender who started behind) scores 2 for the offence. A block or a stall scores 2 for the defence. A goal scores 1.

**What the rules push players to do**

Defenders are paid for giving up the under and stopping the deep, which is the 2s' chosen order of priorities. Cutters learn that the under is what this defence gives.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play Space Invaders, with all four priorities scored.
- 2s: The 2s' game in week 8.

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "Which shoulder were you on when you were beaten?"
- Ask: "What did you give up on purpose?"

**Harder**

- Stall 7, even numbers.

**Easier**

- A spare defender playing deep.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 8.
drills.setup_instructions: 4v4 on a 35 x 20 m pitch with endzones. Person defence, one-way force.

drills.title: Cut-and-clear game
drills.description:
Clearing is part of cutting. In this game the next cut can't start until the last cutter has cleared.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Normal ultimate at stall 8.
2. A cutter who isn't thrown to must clear to the break side before anyone else cuts.
3. A throw to a cutter who went before the lane was clear is a turnover.

**Scoring**

A goal scores 1. A goal caught by a player who cleared earlier in the same possession scores 2.

**What the rules push players to do**

Players run their clear with purpose because the team is waiting for it, and they learn that a clear becomes the next cut.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play vert from the front with the same idea: a goal only counts if the scorer cleared at least once.
- 2s: The 2s' game in week 6.

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "Where do you go when you aren't thrown to?"
- Ask: "How did you know the lane was yours?"

**Harder**

- Stall 6; clears must go through the break side and back to the stack.

**Easier**

- 5v4.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 6.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v5 on a 35 x 25 m pitch in a vertical stack.

drills.title: Sideline trap game
drills.description:
Every possession starts trapped, and the bonus is for punishing the trap rather than surviving it.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Every possession starts on the trap sideline.
2. The defence may call "shift" at stall 5 to shut the dump.

**Scoring**

A goal scores 1. An escape to the break side or the middle within two passes scores a bonus point straight away. A stall on the line scores 1 for the defence.

**What the rules push players to do**

Handlers get the disc off the line before the defence is balanced, and cutters attack the break side and the middle.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' game in week 21.
- 2s: The 2s play the sideline-start game: a goal scored without going back to the starting sideline scores 2.

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "At what stall did you turn to the dump?"
- Ask: "Where did the cutters go to help?"

**Harder**

- The dump defender may poach the first look.

**Easier**

- No shift call.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 21.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v5 on a 30 x 25 m pitch. The disc is checked in on a sideline with a trap mark set and three handlers.
drills.source: Plan; SP Vertical Stack; HN Handler Situations

drills.title: Sideline-start game
drills.description:
The 2s' sideline game: the hardest place to start, over and over, usually with a spare attacker.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phase 1 (technique), Phase 2 (under pressure) and Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Every possession starts on a sideline, and the first pass must leave the line.
2. Stall 7 or 8.

**Scoring**

A goal scores 1. A goal scored without the disc going back to the starting sideline scores 2. In week 40 a give-and-go off the line scores a bonus.

**What the rules push players to do**

The dump or the power-position pass is always on, so players learn to take it early instead of forcing a throw up the line.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play the 3-handler game and the sideline trap game.
- 2s: Weeks 2, 21 and 40.

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "What was your first look on the sideline?"
- Ask: "What did a neutral dump give you?"
- Ask: "What was your first look on the sideline? What did a neutral dump give you?"

**Harder**

- 5v5 at stall 6.

**Easier**

- 5v3, or stall 10 for the first pass.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 2, 21 and 40.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v4 or 5v5 on a 30 x 20 m pitch; later 7v7.

drills.title: Forward-backward stall game
drills.description:
The 2s' first reset game: turning to the dump buys time.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phase 1 (technique) and Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. The stall is 4 if you throw forwards and 10 if you throw backwards.
2. The marker counts to 10; a forward throw after "four" is a turnover.

**Scoring**

A goal scores 1. From week 14 a completed dump and swing scores a bonus point.

**What the rules push players to do**

Players find out for themselves that the dump is never a bad idea, and start looking for it by stall 4.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play positive and negative resets, 2v2.
- 2s: Weeks 1 and 14.

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "What changed when you turned round?"
- Ask: "What did the dump give your team?"
- Ask: "What changed when you turned round? What did the dump give your team?"
- Ask: "Where did the swing take the disc, and what was open there?"

**Harder**

- Stall 3 forwards.

**Easier**

- 5v4.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 1 and 14.
drills.setup_instructions: 4v4 or 5v4 on a 30 x 20 m pitch with endzones.

drills.title: 1v1 from the stack spot
drills.description:
The 1v1 cutting test played as a game, with a live mark on the thrower. Getting open under pressure for the cutter; throwing under pressure for the thrower.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. The cutter has until stall 6 to get open, under or away.
2. The thrower has a live mark and may break it.
3. Rotate one place after every rep.

**Scoring**

A clean catch scores 1 for the cutter. A stop (a stall, a block or an incomplete throw) scores 1 for the defender. First to five.

**What the rules push players to do**

The cutter has to be open while the throw is still possible, and the thrower has to deliver it past a mark. It also means every player has met the trial test's set-up several times before it counts.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Stall 6; in week 21 the disc starts on the sideline and an under only counts if it is caught off the line.
- 2s: Stall 8, and the defender starts a step off.

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "What did the defender take away, and what did that leave you?"
- Ask: "Thrower: when did you know which way they were going?"

**Harder**

- Stall 5; the defender is told under or away.

**Easier**

- The defender starts two steps off.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 14, 16 and 21.
drills.setup_instructions: Fours: thrower, marker, cutter, defender. The cutter starts on a stack spot 15 m from the thrower with the defender on their back shoulder.
drills.source: Season plan, Measuring improvement; Flik L4 Lesson 3; HN 10 Big Drills (Win the Box)

drills.title: Out-of-timeout game
drills.description:
Every possession starts from a timeout, so the set play and the defence against it get many reps.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (set pieces) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Each possession starts from a timeout in one of two spots: mid-pitch at stall 7, or on the endzone line.
2. The offence runs its out-of-timeout play. The defence may double the reset or poach the nearest lane for three seconds.

**Scoring**

Five possessions each; the offence aims to score 3 out of 5.

**What the rules push players to do**

The offence designs its play expecting a poach or a double team, and the defence practises taking the first option away for three seconds.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' game in week 40.
- 2s: Optional for the 2s, with their endzone call only.

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "What did the defence do in the first three seconds?"
- Ask: "What was the second option, and who knew it?"

**Harder**

- The defence chooses its look after seeing the set.

**Easier**

- The defence plays straight person D.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 40.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch.
drills.source: Plan; HN Coach Corner, Time Outs

drills.title: Dominator 3v3
drills.description:
The dominator as a small game: yards gained by give-and-go count as a goal.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phase 2 (under pressure) and Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Stall 5.
2. Play starts at one end; the offence works the disc upfield with short passes and give-and-go.

**Scoring**

A 15 m gain made with give-and-go passes scores as a goal. In week 32 a fourth defender poaches, and a pass to the player the poacher left scores a bonus.

**What the rules push players to do**

The thrower has to move the instant the disc leaves their hand, and the three have to keep the throws stable while moving.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Weeks 16 and 32.
- 2s: The 2s play inside break, then continuation (week 16) and 3v3 possession (week 32).

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "How can two or three players working together help the team move the disc?"
- Ask: "When the poacher came, who was left?"

**Harder**

- A fresh defender every point; a poacher.

**Easier**

- 3v2.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 16 and 32.
drills.setup_instructions: 3v3 on a 20 x 15 m pitch.
drills.source: Plan; Bologna Flying Disc, Dominator; Hildo Bijl 34.2

drills.title: Inside break, then continuation
drills.description:
One reliable break has to lead to the next throw.

**Serves:** Breaking the mark · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Stall 8.
2. Normal play, but see the scoring.

**Scoring**

A goal only counts if the possession had an inside break followed by a pass to a different cutter.

**What the rules push players to do**

The thrower breaks to the receiver's outside shoulder so they can keep running, and the next cutter goes as the first one catches.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play Dominator 3v3.
- 2s: The 2s' game in week 16.

**Coaching points**

- Ask: "Where was the next cutter when the break was caught?"
- Ask: "What made the break easy to continue from?"

**Harder**

- Stall 6.

**Easier**

- 3v2.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 16.
drills.setup_instructions: 3v3 on a 25 x 20 m pitch with endzones, one-way force.
drills.source: Plan; HN 10 Big Drills (Break to a Point); Flik L3 Lesson 2

drills.title: Shared vocabulary
drills.description:
The calls every Herd player uses for resets: dump, mac, zip and dynamic dump. Players say the call as they make the move, so the whole club hears the same words.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Walk through each call: dump, mac, zip, dynamic dump.
2. Then play with defence on the disc only: the handlers move and call each move out loud.
3. Rotate the thrower after every completed call.

**Coaching points**

- Say the call as you move, not after.
- It is never a bad idea to use the dump.
- Ask: "Which call did you hear most? Which one did nobody use?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s add positive and negative resets straight after (week 1).
- 2s: The 2s start from the Five Frisbee Habits and the open-side dump, and meet these calls in the joint session.

**Harder**

- Add a defender on one handler; the call still has to come first.

**Easier**

- Walk it with no mark until every call is right.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 1.
drills.setup_instructions: Fours: thrower, marker and two handlers. One disc per group.

drills.title: Fake-fake-throw
drills.description:
Pivots and fakes that look real. Slow pivots build balance first; then two believable fakes come before every throw.

**Serves:** Breaking the mark · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Slow pivots: pivot over 2-3 seconds keeping your centre of mass over the pivot foot, pause and fake, then speed up.
2. In threes with a passive mark: two fakes before every throw.
3. The marker bites on good fakes and calls them out.

**Coaching points**

- A fake must look like the throw: full arm, eyes and shoulders, the same release point.
- Start every pivot from home position: both hands on the disc, lined up with your centre.
- Ask: "Which fake moved the marker, and what made it look real?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Joint session, week 2.
- 2s: Week 4 throwing block: under a passive mark at stall 7, and the mark calls which fake moved them.

**Harder**

- A live mark at stall 6; only one fake allowed, so it has to be real.
- The marker only bites on fakes that use eyes and shoulders.

**Easier**

- No mark: partner calls which fake looked like a throw.
- Passive mark, one fake.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 2 and 4.
drills.setup_instructions: Pivot foot on a line to start; then threes: thrower, marker, receiver.
drills.source: DK 8.5; UAP Forehand wk 1; HN Next Gen 10 (Pivoting to Break the Mark)

drills.title: Threat position
drills.description:
Catch as a threat: land facing upfield and set up to throw at once, so the marker has to choose a side.

**Serves:** Breaking the mark · Phase 1 (technique) and Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. The receiver catches on the run and lands facing upfield.
2. They pivot once to the break side and throw.
3. Week 15: the cutter V-cuts open then to the break side and catches in the 75-degree window; then off-balance throws.

**Coaching points**

- Set up as if you are about to throw a specific throw, or stay neutral with two hands on the disc.
- A mark is most vulnerable while it is still setting: look to the break side early.
- Ask: "What did the marker have to choose between when you caught?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Week 10: threat position and the 75-degree cutting-through window, 3v3, then Break to a Point.
- 2s: Joint sessions in weeks 2 and 15; the 2s keep a passive mark for longer.

**Harder**

- 3v3 (week 10, 1s): a break caught on the move in the 75-degree window scores 2.

**Easier**

- No marker: catch, land facing upfield, show the throw.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 2, 10 and 15.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes: thrower, cutter, marker. The cutter starts 15 m away.

drills.title: Solving sideline traps
drills.description:
What to do when trapped on the line: square up to the middle and use the reset behind the disc. The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. The thrower squares up to the middle of the pitch.
2. The reset comes behind the disc and bounces back.
3. Then the double-team drill: two markers on the disc.

**Coaching points**

- Get it off early: do not spend four or five seconds looking upfield when trapped.
- Cutters attack the break side and the middle, not the line.
- Ask: "Where was the space once you squared up?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' toolkit block in week 2.
- 2s: The 2s work the same problem through the sideline-start game and sideline power position.

**Harder**

- Two markers stay until stall 6.

**Easier**

- A passive trap mark and no reset defender.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 2.
drills.setup_instructions: Fours on a sideline: thrower, trap mark, reset and reset defender.
drills.source: SP "Throwing – escaping sideline trap"; Flik L3 Lesson 8; HN Handler Situations

drills.title: Catching zones
drills.description:
Which catch to use where: clap catch in the middle zone, crab claw high and low, and which edge to take by spin.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Pairs: clap catches in the middle zone.
2. Crab claw high and low.
3. Then which edge to take by the spin of the disc; finish on the mac line.

**Coaching points**

- Feet first: move your body behind the disc, then hands.
- Two hands whenever you can.
- Ask: "Where do most of your drops start: feet or hands?"

**Harder**

- Catch on the move; the thrower varies height without warning.
- The thrower adds pace and wobble while the catcher moves.

**Easier**

- Shorter distance and floatier throws.
- Static catcher, chest height only.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 3.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs, 10 m apart.

drills.title: Handler weave
drills.description:
Handler movement around the disc, called out loud: "Strike, Swing, Dump, Chill, Fill". The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Run the weave for 10 minutes, calling each role: Strike, Swing, Dump, Chill, Fill.
2. Then play 5v5 where a goal only counts after a dump and a swing.

**Coaching points**

- Be open the moment the thrower turns to you, not before or after.
- Throw or fake forward first, then look to the dump.
- Ask: "What did the dump and swing open up?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' toolkit block in week 3.
- 2s: The 2s play Last player to touch the disc picks it up instead.

**Harder**

- Stall 5 in the 5v5.

**Easier**

- 5v4 in the game.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 3.
drills.setup_instructions: Handlers in a weave across the pitch; then a 5v5 pitch with endzones.

drills.title: Give-and-go in pairs
drills.description:
Throw and move: the first step of the give-and-go, in pairs up the pitch.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Throw to your partner.
2. Sprint three steps.
3. Catch on the move and repeat up the pitch.

**Coaching points**

- Start running as the disc leaves your hand.
- Be smooth, not rushed: if you are travelling, you are rushing.
- Ask: "When did you take your first step?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s meet the same footwork in the dominator drill (week 16).
- 2s: The 2s' drill in week 3; the give-and-go comes back in week 32.

**Harder**

- Add a trailing defender on the thrower.

**Easier**

- Jog the three steps.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 3.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs working up the pitch.

drills.title: Shuttle throw
drills.description:
Throwing and running together: throw, then sprint to the back of the opposite line.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Throw to the front of the opposite line.
2. Sprint to the back of that line.
3. Keep the disc moving; add a second disc when it flows.

**Coaching points**

- Step, flick, point: finish with your arm pointing at the target.
- Throw to where the receiver will be.
- Ask: "Did your throw get worse as you got out of breath? What changed?"

**Harder**

- Longer gap, or forehand only.

**Easier**

- Shorter gap and a jog.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 4.
drills.setup_instructions: Two lines facing each other, 10-15 m apart.

drills.title: Chop stop progression
drills.description:
Stopping and changing direction without a hard plant: the chop stop, then the hockey stop.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Walk, jog, then sprint into a chop stop and plant.
2. Then the hockey stop.
3. Then a 5-10 lateral.

**Coaching points**

- Chop, do not plant: chop your feet, stay low for a moment, push off the outside foot.
- Keep the volume low and rest fully: this is speed, not fitness.
- Ask: "Why chop instead of plant?"

**Harder**

- React to a coach's point instead of a cone.

**Easier**

- Stay at jog pace.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 4.
drills.setup_instructions: Lanes of cones 10 m apart.

drills.title: 1v1 "name your cut"
drills.description:
Getting open when the defender knows what is coming: the cutter calls the cut before running it, then has to win anyway.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. The cutter calls the cut out loud.
2. They run it against a live defender and the thrower hits them if they are open.
3. First to five clean catches; rotate.

**Coaching points**

- Winning takes real acceleration and a real change of direction, not a trick.
- Commit: five or six steps fake the defender, two or three only fake the thrower.
- Ask: "Which cut still worked when they knew it was coming? Why?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' game in week 4; also one of the skill-floor activities for getting open.
- 2s: The 2s play Away-then-under 1v1.

**Harder**

- Stall 5 on the thrower.

**Easier**

- The defender starts a step off.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 4.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes: thrower, cutter, defender. The cutter starts 15 m from the thrower.
drills.source: Flik L4 Lesson 3; Wiggins; Flik L2 Lesson 5

drills.title: Away-then-under 1v1
drills.description:
The 2s' version of 1v1 "name your cut": one cut, away then under, run properly.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. From 15 m the cutter drives away for five or six steps.
2. Then they come under.
3. The defender starts a step off. First to five clean catches; rotate.

**Coaching points**

- The length of the drive is what makes the defender turn their hips.
- Sprint the under; a half-cut is worse than no cut.
- Ask: "How many steps did it take before your defender turned?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play 1v1 "name your cut".
- 2s: The 2s' game in week 4.

**Harder**

- The defender starts on the back shoulder.

**Easier**

- The defender starts two steps off.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 4.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes: thrower, cutter, defender. The cutter starts 15 m from the thrower.
drills.source: Flik L4 Lesson 3; Wiggins; Flik L2 Lesson 5

drills.title: Cut families with a defender
drills.description:
The three cut families against a defender, 2v2, so the thrower has a mark too. The cutter has to be open while the throw is still possible.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. 2v2: thrower and marker, cutter and defender.
2. The cutter runs in-out, out-in and lateral cuts.
3. The defence scores for a stall at 6.

**Coaching points**

- Being open is timing, not just speed.
- Get the defender's hips turned, then attack the space behind them.
- Ask: "When were you open, and could the thrower still throw it?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Week 4: in-out, out-in and lateral, stall 6.
- 2s: The 2s run it as away to open under, then under to away, at stall 8; the defence scores for a stall.

**Harder**

- Stall 5; the defender is told the family.

**Easier**

- Stall 8 and a passive mark.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 4.
drills.setup_instructions: Fours: thrower, marker, cutter, defender.

drills.title: Zig-zag cuts
drills.description:
Change of direction at speed: a chop stop at each cone and five or six hard steps between them.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Run the zig-zag with a chop stop at each cone.
2. Take five or six hard steps between cones.
3. The thrower hits the cutter out of the last cone.

**Coaching points**

- Low, chop, explode.
- Stay low through every turn.
- Ask: "At which cone did you lose speed, and why?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run Five-cone cutting.
- 2s: The 2s' cutting drill in week 4.

**Harder**

- A defender shadows the cutter.

**Easier**

- Jog pace with the same footwork.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 4.
drills.setup_instructions: A zig-zag of cones about 5 m apart; a thrower at the end.

drills.title: Archery
drills.description:
Throwing to a target at three distances, scored. Herd also uses archery scoring for hucks: +2 caught in stride, +1 overthrown, 0 if the cutter has to wait.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Throwers aim at the cone targets at 10, 20 and 30 m.
2. Score a point for landing in the hoop zone.
3. Rotate throwers and retrievers.

**Coaching points**

- Accuracy comes from spin: drive the disc through the target, do not guide it.
- Overthrown beats underthrown.
- Ask: "Which distance cost you most points? What changed in your throw?"

**Harder**

- Smaller hoop zones, or a marker at stall 6.
- 30 and 40 m targets, or across the wind.

**Easier**

- Drop the 30 m target.
- 10 and 20 m targets only.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 5.
drills.setup_instructions: Cone targets at 10, 20 and 30 m; a hoop zone marked at each.

drills.title: Shoulder drill
drills.description:
Cutter and thrower agree the target: the cutter points to the shoulder they want and the thrower hits it there. The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. The cutter runs to the first cone and points to the shoulder they want the disc on.
2. The thrower hits that shoulder.
3. Rotate.

**Coaching points**

- Throw to the shoulder away from the defender.
- Lead the receiver: space, not face.
- Ask: "Which shoulder was safe, and how did you show it?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' throwing block in week 5.
- 2s: The 2s run the Christmas tree throwing drill.

**Harder**

- Add a defender; the cutter points late.

**Easier**

- The cutter calls the shoulder early.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 5.
drills.setup_instructions: Thrower and a line of cutters; a cone 10-15 m out.

drills.title: Vert stack game
drills.description:
The vert stack as a game: cut from the back only, and a pass caught in stride scores a bonus.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Play in a vertical stack; cuts come from the back only.
2. A pass caught in stride (the receiver does not slow down) scores a bonus point.
3. Harder round: a goal only counts if the possession included a cutter-to-cutter pass.

**Coaching points**

- Cut in the lane, recover in the stack.
- Be open just before your teammate catches.
- Ask: "When did the thrower start the throw: on the turn, or after it?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: 5v5, then the harder round with a cutter-to-cutter pass.
- 2s: 5v4 first (cut from the back and clear the lane), then 5v5.

**Harder**

- 5v5 at stall 7.

**Easier**

- 5v3.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 5.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v5 or 5v4 on a 35 x 25 m pitch with endzones, in a vertical stack.

drills.title: Ho game with 3 lives
drills.description:
Horizontal-stack spacing as a game: each team has three turnovers before the point ends, and two cutters in the same lane costs a life.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Play in a ho stack. Each team has three lives (turnovers) before the point ends.
2. Two cutters in the same lane costs a life.
3. 7v7 round: two lives and stall 6.

**Coaching points**

- Only the pair in front of the disc is active; the rest stay wide.
- Never more than two in a space.
- Ask: "Who was the active pair, and how did everyone else know?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' game in week 6.
- 2s: The 2s play the Static-start game in vert.

**Harder**

- Two lives.

**Easier**

- Four lives.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 6.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v5 (then 7v7) in a horizontal stack on a wide pitch with endzones.

drills.title: Zipper
drills.description:
The 1s' first ho cutting pattern: away, under, then up-and-under, followed by a walk-through of ho spacing. The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Run the pattern: away, under, then up-and-under.
2. Walk ho spacing: the two in front of the disc cut, the rest stay wide.

**Coaching points**

- Use horo shapes, not vert shapes.
- Clear wide so the next pair has the space.
- Ask: "Who was the active pair when the disc moved?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' drill in week 6.
- 2s: The 2s run Triangle cutting.

**Harder**

- Add defenders on the active pair.

**Easier**

- Walk it with a coach calling each cut.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 6.
drills.setup_instructions: A horizontal stack set against cones; no defence to start.
drills.source: SP; SP "Horizontal stack 1"; Flik L3 Lesson 4

drills.title: Vert from the front
drills.description:
The vert stack cutting from the front, with a third handler: the front of the stack is an upfield reset and cuts go away or across.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phase 1 (technique) and Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. 5v5: the front of the stack cuts first and clears wide.
2. A goal only counts if the scorer cleared at least once in the possession.
3. Week 21 walk-through: 3H as the upfield reset, offset lateral cuts into the undefended channel; then 7v7 with every possession starting on the trap sideline.

**Coaching points**

- The first cut has to be real, or the defender will not move.
- A lateral throw to the 3H gains yards and opens the break side.
- Ask: "What did the first cut open, even when it was not thrown to?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' second offence: weeks 6 and 21.
- 2s: The 2s cut from the back as their default and meet the front version in week 34 (3H shape).

**Harder**

- Stall 6; every possession starts on the trap sideline.

**Easier**

- 5v4.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 6 and 21.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v5 or 7v7 in a vertical stack with three handlers (3H).
drills.source: SP; Flik L3 Lesson 5; HN Flik, Upfield Dump and Undefended Channel; HN Flik, Vertical Stack Sideline; Plan

drills.title: Static-start game
drills.description:
The 2s' stack game: every possession restarts with the stack set, and two cutters in the same lane is a turnover.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Every possession restarts with the stack set.
2. Two cutters in the same lane is a turnover.
3. Play 5v4, then 7v7 in vert.

**Coaching points**

- One cutter, one clear.
- Move the stack with the disc.
- Ask: "Where do you go when you aren't thrown to?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play the Ho game with 3 lives.
- 2s: The 2s' game in week 6.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 6.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v4, then 7v7, in a vertical stack on a pitch with endzones.

drills.title: Triangle cutting
drills.description:
A cutting pattern for three cutters, then the same pattern as a team (team triangle cutting). The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Run triangle cutting in threes with a thrower.
2. Then team triangle cutting.

**Coaching points**

- Your clear is a cut: run it hard.
- Time your cut to be open as the thrower looks.
- Ask: "Where did you go when you were not thrown to?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run the Zipper.
- 2s: The 2s' drill in week 6.

**Harder**

- Add a defender on each cutter.

**Easier**

- Walk the pattern first.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 6.
drills.setup_instructions: Cones for a three-cutter triangle; a thrower.
drills.source: SP; SP "Horizontal stack 1"; Flik L3 Lesson 4

drills.title: Marking with intensity
drills.description:
Marking with a job: the thrower names their favourite throw, the mark takes it away, and the thrower rates the mark's intensity. It goes with theory Card 27.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. The thrower names their favourite throw.
2. The mark takes it away, one side at a time.
3. The thrower rates the mark's intensity 1-3. Rotate.

**Coaching points**

- Go into the mark at full intensity and try to win there.
- Hands with a job: place them, do not wave them.

**Harder**

- The thrower may use both sides.

**Easier**

- The thrower names the throw before each rep.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 7.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes: thrower, mark, receiver.

drills.title: Marking base
drills.description:
The athletic marking base, from static to moving: hold the base, hop into it, shuffle and reach without shifting your weight.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Base hold, then hop into base.
2. 5 m side shuffle with a pause and a reach.
3. Marker movement with hands clasped: ten touches, then swap.

**Coaching points**

- Feet slightly wider than shoulders, weight on the balls of your feet, hips back, eyes on the thrower.
- Reach without shifting your weight.
- Ask: "Where was your weight when you reached?"

**Harder**

- React to a partner's pivot instead of a count.

**Easier**

- Shorter shuffles and longer pauses.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 7.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs with 5 m of space each side.
drills.source: UAP Marking wk 1; Flik L4 Lesson 7; HN Practice Sessions 3 (Forcing the disc)

drills.title: Triangle mark game
drills.description:
The triangle mark under real throws: the defence scores for what a good mark produces.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Play small-sided ultimate; every mark is a triangle mark.
2. Joint: the defence scores for a stall or a point block.
3. 1s, 4v4: the defence also scores for a possession with no break thrown.

**Coaching points**

- Shown throw with hand, around with body, inside with shoulder.
- Make the thrower spend the stall pivoting instead of reading the field.
- Ask: "Which throw were you taking away first? How did the thrower try to change that?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: 4v4, with a point for any possession where no break is thrown.
- 2s: The 2s play the Tram-line game.

**Harder**

- 5v5 with a live dump.

**Easier**

- The defence also scores for a throw kept to the forced side.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 7.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v5 (joint) or 4v4 (1s) on a 30 x 20 m pitch with endzones.

drills.title: Triangle marking progression
drills.description:
The triangle mark built up in three steps: no pivot, one pivot, then the full triangle drill.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Zero-pivot drill.
2. One-pivot drill.
3. The full triangle drill: a win for the mark is any throw that does not hit the cutter in stride.

**Coaching points**

- Stop the shown throw, move your feet to stop the first pivot, drop deeper for the second, then recover.
- Take the dangerous throw first, then close.
- Ask: "Which pivot beat you, the first or the second?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' throwing block in week 7.
- 2s: The 2s run Marker movement one way.

**Harder**

- The thrower may use two pivots.

**Easier**

- Stay on the one-pivot drill.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 7.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes: thrower, mark, cutter.
drills.source: UAP Marking wk 4; Flik L2 Lesson 7; HN Point of Attack

drills.title: Marker movement one way
drills.description:
Holding a one-way force: the 2s' first marking drill, followed by Flik's 3-person drill modified.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. The mark holds a one-way force for five throws.
2. Rotate.
3. Then the 3-person drill modified.

**Coaching points**

- Move your feet first, then your hands.
- Eyes on the thrower, not the disc.
- Ask: "What got past you: the around or the inside?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run the Triangle marking progression.
- 2s: The 2s' throwing block in week 7.

**Harder**

- The thrower may pivot twice.

**Easier**

- The thrower may not fake.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 7.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes: thrower, mark, receiver.
drills.source: UAP Marking wk 4; Flik L2 Lesson 7

drills.title: Drop step and W drill
drills.description:
Defensive footwork: backpedal, drop step and open the hips, then the W pattern and defensive turning.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Backpedal, drop step, open your hips.
2. Run the W pattern through the cones.
3. Then defensive turning.

**Coaching points**

- Never turn your back on the disc.
- Build speed in stages: sidestep, crossover, sprint.
- Ask: "Which way did you turn, and could you still see your player?"

**Harder**

- React to a partner instead of the cones.

**Easier**

- Walk the drop step first.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 8.
drills.setup_instructions: A W of five cones, about 5 m between them.

drills.title: Buffering
drills.description:
Keeping the buffer: the "string from belly button to belly button" between defender and cutter. The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Jog, then full pace, keeping the string between you and the cutter.
2. Then the diamond drill.

**Coaching points**

- Choose the space you are protecting and keep a buffer to it.
- You react; you do not act.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' drill in week 8.
- 2s: The 2s run Mirror defending.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 8.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs: cutter and defender in a 10 m lane; then the diamond drill.
drills.source: Flik L4 Lesson 6; UAP Defence wk 3; Flik L2 Lesson 8

drills.title: 2v2 deep space
drills.description:
Protecting the deep space first: two defenders stop the deep, then the under.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. 2v2: the defence must stop the deep first, then the under.
2. Then Blocks Only, 5v5.

**Coaching points**

- Stand on the back shoulder: deep first, then fight the under.
- Follow the under with your hips; do not let them turn you around.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Stall 6 on the thrower.
- 2s: Stall 8, and in Blocks Only any touch by the defence counts.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 8.
drills.setup_instructions: 2v2 in a long lane with a thrower; then 5v5.

drills.title: Zig-zag and tunnel drills
drills.description:
Defensive footwork for the 2s: staying with a cutter through changes of direction, then Blocks Only. The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Zig-zag: the defender stays with a cutter changing direction at each cone.
2. Tunnel: the defender keeps position on a cutter running a narrow lane.
3. Then Blocks Only, 5v5, where any touch by the defence counts.

**Coaching points**

- Low, fast feet, head up.
- Drop-step and open your hips; never turn your back on the disc.
- Ask: "Where did you lose your player?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run 2v2 deep space.
- 2s: The 2s' toolkit block in week 8.

**Harder**

- Full pace with a thrower.

**Easier**

- Jog pace.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 8.
drills.setup_instructions: A zig-zag of cones and a tunnel of cones for each pair.

drills.title: Star drill
drills.description:
Reaction work for defenders and marks, done early in the session while players are fresh. The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. The star drill with a tennis ball.
2. Then reactive marking: marks react to a point, a voice or a fake from the coach.

**Coaching points**

- React, do not guess: hold your base until the thrower commits.
- Only move your feet when they move theirs.

**Harder**

- Two balls, or a later call.

**Easier**

- An earlier drop.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 9.
drills.setup_instructions: A star of cones around the defender; a tennis ball per pair.
drills.source: UAP Defence wk 4; UAP Marking wk 3

drills.title: Break force and cutting with hand calls
drills.description:
Thrower and receiver read each other: the thrower breaks the mark only on the receiver's hand call.

**Serves:** Breaking the mark · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. The marker sets a force.
2. The receiver cuts and gives a hand call.
3. The thrower breaks the mark only on that call.

**Coaching points**

- Watch the body, not the disc.
- A break should lead to a throw that gains yards next.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 9.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes: thrower, marker, receiver.

drills.title: True mark v 45-degree flat mark shuffles
drills.description:
Footwork for two marks: shuffling in a true mark and in a 45-degree flat mark, before the 1s learn the flat mark on a call. The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Shuffle in a true mark.
2. Shuffle in a 45-degree flat mark.
3. Swap after each set.

**Coaching points**

- Shoulders and hips parallel to the endzone in the flat mark.
- Stay on your toes, ready to move either way.
- Ask: "What changes for your feet between the two marks?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' throwing block in week 9.
- 2s: The 2s run Reaction pairs.

**Harder**

- A partner calls the mark to switch mid-set.

**Easier**

- Hold each mark still before shuffling.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 9.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs: thrower and mark.

drills.title: Flat mark
drills.description:
The BFD flat mark, which every 1s player can switch to on a call: walked through, then set up in the chaos of the first seconds.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Walk through the flat mark: shoulders and hips parallel to the endzone.
2. Then the Best Breakmark drill: the handler receives a short pass and moves, so the mark sets up in the first seconds.
3. The dishing player calls travels.

**Coaching points**

- Close down on the first threatened throw, then stay within 3 m for the second.
- On the call, everyone downfield knows the open side has changed.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' toolkit block in week 9.
- 2s: The 2s do not need the flat mark yet.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 9.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes: dishing player, handler, mark.
drills.source: BFD; HN Point of Attack; Flik L4 Lesson 8

drills.title: Reaction pairs
drills.description:
Reaction work for the 2s' marks: mirror a partner, then react to a thrower's fakes.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Mirror drill in pairs.
2. Then the mark reacts to the thrower's fakes for 30 seconds.
3. Swap.

**Coaching points**

- Eyes, hips, shoulders show the throw before the disc moves.
- React, do not guess.
- Ask: "Which cue told you the throw was real?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run the mark shuffles.
- 2s: The 2s' throwing block in week 9.

**Harder**

- 40 seconds, with a live throw at the end.

**Easier**

- 20 seconds and slower fakes.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 9.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs facing each other.

drills.title: Mark and downfield D together
drills.description:
The mark and the downfield defenders working as one: the force sets what the defenders protect.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. 2v2 with a mark on the thrower.
2. The defence scores for a stall at 8 or a throw into the downfield defender.

**Coaching points**

- A mark that forces hard makes every other defender's job easier.
- Downfield: keep your back to the open side.
- Ask: "Mark: what did you take away? Downfield: did you know?"
- Ask: "Where did the mark send the throw? Was someone there?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play the Mark-call game.
- 2s: The 2s' game in week 9.

**Harder**

- Stall 6.

**Easier**

- A third defender.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 9.
drills.setup_instructions: 2v2 downfield with a thrower and a mark.

drills.title: Wide and low releases
drills.description:
Width and height beat the mark: step out wide to release, then release low under a pool noodle.

**Serves:** Breaking the mark · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. Wide release: step out past a cone to release and hold the finish for 2 seconds. Widen the cone each round.
2. Low release under a pool noodle held at hip height.
3. The marker says "ding" if the disc is above it; the height can change rep to rep.

**Coaching points**

- Wide, low, hold it.
- Hold your finish for two seconds to prove your balance.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 10.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs with a cone to step past; a pool noodle per group.
drills.source: Flik L4 Lesson 1; Plan; HN Practice Sessions 5

drills.title: Sideways game
drills.description:
Herd's version of the Sideways game: most throws are lateral, so the around break is the way forward.

**Serves:** Breaking the mark · Phase 1 (technique).

**How it runs**

1. 4v4, one-way force.
2. Teams score in the endzones on either sideline.
3. Most throws are lateral, so the around break moves the disc.

**Coaching points**

- Step out and throw the around past the marker's foot.
- Lateral cutters: keep moving into the break side.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play threat position and the cutting-through window, 3v3.
- 2s: The 2s' game in week 10.

**Harder**

- Stall 6.

**Easier**

- 5v4.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 10.
drills.setup_instructions: 4v4 on a pitch wider than it is long, with an endzone along each sideline.
drills.source: Plan; BFD; HN 10 Big Drills; Flik L3 Lesson 1

drills.title: Throwing ladder
drills.description:
The restart after the break: climb the ladder from stable flat throws to quick catch-and-release.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Stable flat throws.
2. Pivots and fakes, then IO and OI, then high and low releases.
3. Finish with quick catch-and-release in pairs (Quick throwing).

**Coaching points**

- Do not climb a rung until the last one is stable.
- Step, flick, point.
- Ask: "Which rung broke down first after three weeks off?"

**Harder**

- Add a passive mark from the pivots rung.

**Easier**

- Stay on a rung for longer.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 14.
drills.setup_instructions: Mixed groups of four or five, in pairs or lines.

drills.title: Line cutting drill
drills.description:
Getting open against a tight defender with two threats.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. The runner fakes between the two inner cones.
2. They win by reaching an outer cone 2 m ahead of the defender.
3. Then add a thrower 10 m away.

**Coaching points**

- Get the defender's hips turned, then go.
- You choose when the race starts.

**Harder**

- The defender starts level.

**Easier**

- The runner gets a 1 m start.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 14.
drills.setup_instructions: Two inner cones and two outer cones in a line; later a thrower 10 m away.

drills.title: Finding dump spaces
drills.description:
Setting up the reset quickly wherever the force is.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. The marker picks a force at the check.
2. The dump has 3 seconds to set up.
3. Play the reset out; rotate.

**Coaching points**

- Negative on the open side, positive on the break side.
- Always keep at least two threats.
- Ask: "Where did you set, and which two threats did that give you?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' drill in week 14.
- 2s: The 2s run Dump swing.

**Harder**

- Add a dump defender who may poach the first look.

**Easier**

- 5 seconds to set up.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 14.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes or fours: thrower, marker, dump (and dump defender).

drills.title: Ho cutting shapes
drills.description:
The cuts the horizontal stack uses, one at a time. The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. 45-degree open-side dump.
2. Away to open under.
3. Away to break under.

**Coaching points**

- Use horo shapes, not vert shapes.
- Only the pair in front of the disc is active.
- Ask: "Which shape gave the thrower the easiest throw?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' drill in week 15.
- 2s: The 2s run the around throw to a lateral cut.

**Harder**

- Add defenders on the active pair.

**Easier**

- Walk each shape first.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 15.
drills.setup_instructions: A horizontal stack against cones, with a thrower and a dump.

drills.title: Break to the active pair
drills.description:
Breaking the mark inside the ho: only the two cutters in front of the disc may receive the first pass.

**Serves:** Breaking the mark · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. 5v5 in ho.
2. Only the two cutters in front of the disc may receive the first pass.
3. A break to either scores a bonus point.

**Coaching points**

- Look to the break side early in the stall.
- After one break, look for the next throw that gains yards.
- Ask: "What did the other two cutters do to help?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' game in week 15.
- 2s: The 2s play the Break Force Game, harder.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 15.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v5 in a horizontal stack on a pitch with endzones.
drills.source: HN Flik, Horizontal Stack; Ian French (Break-Throw Bonus Point)

drills.title: Ho spacing walk-through
drills.description:
Who cuts in the ho: the two in front of the disc, one on each side of the thrower.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Walk who cuts: the two in front of the disc, one on each side of the thrower.
2. Then 7v7 in ho with live breaks to the active pair.

**Coaching points**

- Cutters about 9 m apart, 8-12 m from the disc.
- The rest stay wide and out of the lanes.
- Ask: "Who is active when the disc is on the sideline?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' toolkit block in week 15.
- 2s: The 2s run Vert initiation.

**Harder**

- The defence poaches off the far cutter.

**Easier**

- Freeze after each pass and reset the spacing.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 15.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch.
drills.source: HN Flik, Horizontal Stack; HN Flik, Initiating Movement

drills.title: Vert initiation
drills.description:
How the 2s start the vert stack: a set order for the first three cuts.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Front of stack cuts open, then break.
2. Second goes deep, then open under. Third cuts under.
3. Then 7v7 in vert, score on a break, with the Golden Arm rotation.

**Coaching points**

- One cutter, one clear.
- Cut in the lane, recover in the stack.
- Ask: "What does the second cutter watch before going?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run the Ho spacing walk-through.
- 2s: The 2s' toolkit block in week 15.

**Harder**

- The defence knows the order.

**Easier**

- Walk the three cuts, then jog them.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 15.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch in a vertical stack.

drills.title: Dominator from the ho
drills.description:
The 1s' dominator set: two or three handlers play give-and-go in front while cutters clear vertically.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Walk it: two or three handlers play give-and-go in front; cutters clear vertically.
2. The cutters become options when the handlers stop.
3. Then 7v7 in ho, with the dominator called whenever the disc stalls.

**Coaching points**

- Catch and immediately fake or throw; after the throw, start running.
- Cutters time their entry for when the handlers stop.
- Ask: "When the handlers stopped, who was the first option?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' toolkit block in week 16.
- 2s: The 2s run Break to a Point.

**Harder**

- A poaching defender sits in the handler space.

**Easier**

- 5v5 with no stall on the first three passes.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 16.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch in a horizontal stack.
drills.source: BFD, Dominator; HN Team Analysis, PoNY 2021; HN 10 Big Drills; DK ch. 7

drills.title: Break to a Point
drills.description:
Break the mark to a spot: hit the cutter in stride at a break-side cone, then the next cutter goes.

**Serves:** Breaking the mark · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. The cutter runs to a break-side cone; the thrower hits them in stride.
2. The next cutter goes as the first one catches.
3. Turnovers are fine: throw it.

**Coaching points**

- Break to the receiver's outside shoulder so they can keep running.
- Width and height beat the mark.
- Ask: "Where was the next cutter when the break was caught?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Week 10, after the cutting-through window game.
- 2s: Week 16: then 7v7 in vert, recovering one incomplete break per point.

**Harder**

- Stall 5 on the thrower.

**Easier**

- A passive mark.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 16.
drills.setup_instructions: Thrower, marker and a line of cutters; a cone on the break side.

drills.title: Battle for field sense
drills.description:
Seeing more than your own player: two runners cross and the defenders decide whether to switch, then heads-up D.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (team defence) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Two runners cross with defenders who decide whether to switch.
2. Then the four-cut-point drill: steal looks without losing your player.

**Coaching points**

- Steal a look when your player is stationary, has committed to a line, or is clearing.
- Call it early and by name.
- Ask: "When was it safe to look away from your player?"

**Harder**

- Add a thrower; a wrong switch is a free catch.

**Easier**

- Walk the crossing and call it out loud.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 17.
drills.setup_instructions: Two runners and two defenders in a 15 m box; then four cut points for heads-up D.

drills.title: 3v2 game (perpetual attacker)
drills.description:
Two defenders against three attackers: one offence player in a bib stays on offence all the time, so the defenders have to talk and switch.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (team defence) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Play 3v2 with one perpetual offence player in a bib.
2. The defence scores for a stall or a turnover.
3. Rotate the bib every few points.

**Coaching points**

- Take away the dangerous option first, then help.
- Talk: say who you have.
- Ask: "What did you say to each other, and when?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Stall 6.
- 2s: Stall 8.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 17.
drills.setup_instructions: 3v2 on a small pitch with endzones; one bib.

drills.title: Last-back poach practice
drills.description:
Poaching from the stack: the last back, the front of the stack and flash poaches. The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (team defence) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Last-back poach practice.
2. Front-of-stack defence.
3. Flash poaches from the stack.

**Coaching points**

- Leave just long enough to deny one throw, then recover.
- If one person poaches, everyone shifts.
- Ask: "What three things were true before you left your player?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' drill in week 17.
- 2s: The 2s run Picking up players.

**Harder**

- Live 7v7 with a poach bonus.

**Easier**

- Walk each poach with the offence frozen.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 17.
drills.setup_instructions: A vertical stack with defenders; a thrower and a mark.
drills.source: HN Amsterdam Conference, Developing Great Defenders; HN Excel Premium; HN Team Defence; HN Practice Sessions 11

drills.title: Team defence by stack
drills.description:
How the defence sets against each stack, so everyone knows the plan before the first pass.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (team defence) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Against vert: a 45-degree mark and a dump-defender poach.
2. Against ho: a flatter mark and the open-side handler defender sags. The last back talks.
3. Then 7v7: the offence alternates vert and ho, and the defence must call the stack before the first pass.

**Coaching points**

- Everyone knows the plan: without one, poaching just looks lazy.
- The last back talks.
- Ask: "Who called the stack, and how early?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' toolkit block in week 17.
- 2s: The 2s run Poach and clog near the disc.

**Harder**

- The offence may change stack mid-point.

**Easier**

- The offence says which stack it is in.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 17.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch.
drills.source: HN Point of Attack; HN Flik, Marking vs Stacks; HN Excel Premium, Handler Switching

drills.title: Picking up players
drills.description:
Picking up players moving through your area, then doing it with a sideways body position so you can see the disc. The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (team defence) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Defenders pick up players moving through their area.
2. Then with a sideways body position.

**Coaching points**

- Pick up the next player as soon as you leave the last.
- Head on a swivel: see the disc and your player.
- Ask: "Who did you pick up, and who told you?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run Last-back poach practice.
- 2s: The 2s' drill in week 17.

**Harder**

- Add a thrower who may hit any free attacker.

**Easier**

- Attackers walk.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 17.
drills.setup_instructions: Defenders hold areas while attackers move through them.
drills.source: HN Amsterdam Conference, Developing Great Defenders; HN Team Defence; HN Practice Sessions 11

drills.title: Poach and clog near the disc
drills.description:
The 2s' team defence: the open-side dump defender poaches the lane and the mark rolls with the disc.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (team defence) · Phase 2 (under pressure) and Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Walk it: the open-side dump defender poaches the lane.
2. The mark rolls with the disc (handler switch).
3. Then 7v7 with a poach bonus; the offence plays Three new handlers.

**Coaching points**

- Clog their lane, then find your player.
- If one person poaches, everyone shifts.
- Ask: "When you poached, who covered your player?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run Team defence by stack.
- 2s: The 2s' toolkit block in weeks 17 and 33.

**Harder**

- Week 33: against the 1s' offence if both squads share a pitch.

**Easier**

- Freeze the offence and walk each shift.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 17 and 33.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch.
drills.source: HN Point of Attack; HN Flik, Marking vs Stacks; HN Excel Premium, Handler Switching

drills.title: Circle throwing
drills.description:
A trial drill that is new to everyone: hit the player opposite, past one, then two, then three defenders.

**Serves:** Seeing the field · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Throwers stand in a big circle.
2. Each must hit the player opposite.
3. Add defenders inside the circle: one, then two, then three.

**Coaching points**

- Look before you catch.
- Close is not covered: check the defender's hips.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 19.
drills.setup_instructions: Throwers in a big circle; defenders inside it.

drills.title: Field-assessment drill
drills.description:
Read, then throw: catch with your back to the field, turn, read the deep defender and throw long to the safe shoulder.

**Serves:** Seeing the field · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. A cutter with their back to the field cuts in for a gut pass.
2. They turn and read which side the deep defender is on.
3. They throw long to the safe shoulder.

**Coaching points**

- Read, process, move: do the reading before you catch.
- Overthrown beats underthrown.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 19.
drills.setup_instructions: Thrower, cutter, a deep receiver and a deep defender.

drills.title: Defensive positioning drill
drills.description:
A trial drill for downfield defence: the cutter attacks each cone to get to the open side, and the defender stops them.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. The cutter attacks each cone of the box, trying to get to the open side.
2. The defender stops them.
3. The thrower throws if the cutter is open. Rotate.

**Coaching points**

- Take away the first option, every time.
- Low, fast feet, head up, pick your spot.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 20.
drills.setup_instructions: A box of four cones in front of a thrower.

drills.title: Throws against a trap
drills.description:
The throws that get the disc off a trapped sideline, each for a few minutes.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Big around backhand, big around forehand.
2. IO forehand; IO high and low backhands.
3. Fast off-hand pass.

**Coaching points**

- Square up to the middle first.
- Wide, low, hold it.
- Ask: "Which of these throws would you trust at stall 6 on the line?"

**Harder**

- Add a trap mark at stall 5.

**Easier**

- Drop the off-hand pass.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 21.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs on a sideline.

drills.title: Quickly setting up the dump
drills.description:
Resetting on the line again and again, then against the defence's "shift" call.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. The dump runs up the line and catches.
2. The thrower immediately sets up as the new dump.
3. Then the marker calls "shift" at stall 5 and the dump defender closes the upfield option.

**Coaching points**

- Expect the shift around stall 5, so dump earlier.
- Off the line, then attack.
- Ask: "At what stall did you turn to the dump?"

**Harder**

- The shift may come at stall 3.

**Easier**

- No shift call.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 21.
drills.setup_instructions: Fours on a sideline: thrower, marker, dump, dump defender.

drills.title: 3H cutting
drills.description:
Cuts for the third handler in the vert stack, then the 3H clear-dump power play. The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. 3H cutting.
2. Then the 3H clear-dump power play.

**Coaching points**

- The front of the stack is an upfield reset.
- Off the line, then attack.
- Ask: "What did the 3H's cut open for the next throw?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' drill in week 21.
- 2s: The 2s run the Sideline wrinkle.

**Harder**

- Start every rep on the trap sideline.

**Easier**

- Walk it with no defence.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 21.
drills.setup_instructions: A vertical stack with three handlers.
drills.source: SP Vertical Stack; Flik L3 Lesson 8

drills.title: Vert on the sideline
drills.description:
Where the vert stack stands when the disc is on the line: angled to face the disc so both lanes stay open.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Walk it: angle the stack to face the disc so both lanes stay open.
2. Then 7v7 in vert starting on the sideline, with Three new handlers.

**Coaching points**

- Move the stack with the disc.
- Getting off the sideline is the only priority.
- Ask: "Which lane was open once the stack turned?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run Vert from the front.
- 2s: The 2s' toolkit block in week 21.

**Harder**

- A trap mark and stall 6.

**Easier**

- Freeze and reset the stack after each pass.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 21.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch, disc on a sideline.

drills.title: Five-pass game
drills.description:
Quick disc processing in a tiny space: five passes at stall 5, winner stays on.

**Serves:** Seeing the field · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. 3v3 in a 10 x 10 m square at stall 5.
2. Five completed passes wins.
3. Winner stays on.

**Coaching points**

- Look before you catch.
- Move as you throw.
- Ask: "What did you know before the disc reached you?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Same game; the 1s keep stall 5 and may shrink the square.
- 2s: Same game; the 2s may start at stall 6.

**Harder**

- 3v3 in 8 x 8 m.

**Easier**

- 12 x 12 m.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 22.
drills.setup_instructions: 3v3 in a 10 x 10 m square.

drills.title: Positioning the vertical stack
drills.description:
Where the vert stack moves as the disc swings and moves downfield, then string: the first and second cuts are called. The plan gives this in outline; check the full version in its source before running it.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Walk the stack's position as the disc swings and moves downfield.
2. Then string: the first and second cuts are called, so continuation knows who to look for.

**Coaching points**

- Move the stack with the disc.
- The stack is where you recover, not where you cut.
- Ask: "Where is the stack when the disc is on the far sideline?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run Peppermills.
- 2s: The 2s' drill in week 22.

**Harder**

- Live defence, and the disc may be swung at any time.

**Easier**

- Use cones for each disc position.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 22.
drills.setup_instructions: A vertical stack with a thrower and a dump; cones for disc positions.
drills.source: SP Horizontal Stack 2 and 4; SP Vertical Stack; HN Excel Premium

drills.title: Fast-break game
drills.description:
The first three seconds after a turn: the coach's whistle is a turnover and the closest player picks up.

**Serves:** Seeing the field · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Play 4v4.
2. The coach's whistle is a turnover; the closest player picks up.
3. A goal within 10 seconds of the whistle scores 2.

**Coaching points**

- Look, then pick up: choose your target before you touch the disc.
- On defence, whoever is nearest marks and everyone states the force.
- Ask: "What did you see before you picked the disc up?"
- Ask: "Who did you pick before you picked it up?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play the Banana play against a deep poach.
- 2s: The 2s' game in week 22.

**Harder**

- A goal must come within 8 seconds.
- The whistle goes with the disc deep in the offence's own end.

**Easier**

- 5v4 for the team that wins the disc.
- Pick up from the middle.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 22.
drills.setup_instructions: 4v4 on a 30 x 20 m pitch with endzones.
drills.source: HN Flik, Banana; HN Coach Corner, Fast Break Principles

drills.title: Endzone setup and endzone play
drills.description:
Setting up fast near the endzone, then scoring from 10 m with the "Endzone" and "Spread" calls.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (endzone) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. 7v7 jogs; the disc is dropped and the new offence sets up the endzone stack.
2. 4v4 from 10 m out, aiming to score 4 out of 5.
3. 7v7 "Spread" reps: three handlers dominate at the front, four spread across the back, and the defence is told to poach.

**Coaching points**

- Come wide, set fast.
- If their defenders sag in, hit the spread receiver.
- Ask: "Who set up first, and where did the fourth player go?"

**Harder**

- Stall 6 from the set.

**Easier**

- Score 3 out of 5.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 23.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch; then 4v4 from 10 m out.

drills.title: Fielding the pull
drills.description:
Receiving the pull: the "1" secures it and the "2" centres it, against a chasing defender.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (set pieces) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. The "1" moves forwards onto the pull and secures it.
2. The "2" checks their shoulder, gets open and centres it.
3. Reps against a chasing defender.

**Coaching points**

- First look, then backup.
- After the centring pass the disc should usually go upfield quickly.
- Ask: ""2": what did you see when you checked your shoulder?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Same drill; the 1s go straight into the ho pull play.
- 2s: Same drill; the 2s go straight into the vert pull play.

**Harder**

- Two chasers.
- Bladey pulls and a fast chase.

**Easier**

- No chaser for the first reps.
- The coach throws a short pull.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 23.
drills.setup_instructions: A puller, a "1" and a "2", and a chasing defender.

drills.title: Ho pull play (the slash)
drills.description:
The 1s' first pull play from the horizontal stack, walked then live.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (set pieces) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. The two central cutters slash to the break side.
2. The break-side cutter attacks the cleared space or bounces back for a 7-cut.
3. Walk it, then run it live from a pull.

**Coaching points**

- Every pull play has an ideal output and a backup.
- When it dies, swing into the system.
- Ask: "What was the backup, and who started it?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' drill in week 23, with Windmill under and away.
- 2s: The 2s run the Vert pull play.

**Harder**

- The defence knows the play.

**Easier**

- Walk it twice before running it.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 23.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch from a pull.
drills.source: HN Excel Premium, Dynamic Pull Plays

drills.title: Vert pull play
drills.description:
The 2s' pull play from the vertical stack: the rest of the stack clears so the front of the stack can cut deep.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (set pieces) · Phase 2 (under pressure) and Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. The rest of the stack clears to the sidelines.
2. The front of the stack cuts deep.
3. Walk it, then run it live from a pull.

**Coaching points**

- Every pull play has an ideal output and a backup.
- Do not hang out in the deep space when it dies.
- Ask: "If the deep cut is covered, what is next?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run the Ho pull play.
- 2s: The 2s' drill in week 23. Week 28 runs it as a 5-pull: a goal within five passes scores 2.

**Harder**

- A goal within five passes scores 2.

**Easier**

- Walk it twice before running it.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 23 and 28.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch from a pull.
drills.source: HN Excel Premium, Dynamic Pull Plays

drills.title: Pull play into system
drills.description:
What happens when the pull play dies: the defence takes away the first look on purpose.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (set pieces) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. 7v7 from a pull.
2. The defence takes away the first look on purpose.
3. If it is covered, swing to flip the field and play the system.

**Coaching points**

- When it dies, swing into your system.
- Do not clog the front of the stack or hang deep.
- Ask: "How did the line know the play had died?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' toolkit block in week 23.
- 2s: The 2s run Endzone basics.

**Harder**

- The defence may choose which look to take away.

**Easier**

- The defence says what it is taking away.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 23.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch from a pull.
drills.source: HN Excel Premium, Transitioning to your System

drills.title: String
drills.description:
The 2s' called play: the first and second cuts are named, so continuation knows who to look for.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (set pieces) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Call the first and second cuts.
2. Walk it through.
3. Then 5-pull with the play called in the huddle.

**Coaching points**

- Know the plan, hear the word.
- The second cut goes as the first one catches.
- Ask: "Who was the second cut, and when did they go?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s use the ho pull plays.
- 2s: The 2s' set piece from week 22; walked again in week 23.

**Harder**

- The defence hears the call.

**Easier**

- Walk it twice before the 5-pull.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 23.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch.
drills.source: SP Horizontal Stack 6; SP Vertical Stack

drills.title: Endzone basics
drills.description:
The 2s' endzone set: vert stack, open-side cone, upfield dump.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (endzone) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Walk it: vert stack, open-side cone, upfield dump.
2. Then Redzone Continuous on a 20 m pitch.

**Coaching points**

- Come wide, set fast.
- Reset patiently rather than forcing the first cut.
- Ask: "Where does the fourth player to arrive go?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run Pull play into system.
- 2s: The 2s' toolkit block in week 23.

**Harder**

- Stall 6.

**Easier**

- 5v4 in Redzone Continuous.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 23.
drills.setup_instructions: A 20 m pitch with an endzone.
drills.source: HN Flik, Endzone Offence; Ian French (Redzone Continuous)

drills.title: Zone with a CRUMBLE call
drills.description:
Switching from the Bull zone to person defence on the CRUMBLE call.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (zones) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Walk the transition to person defence on the call, matching up deepest first.
2. Then 7v7 where the captain calls CRUMBLE at any moment.

**Coaching points**

- Echo every call.
- Pick up the deepest offensive players first; when in doubt, leave the thrower unmarked.
- Ask: "Who did you pick up, and who was left?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' toolkit block in week 24.
- 2s: The 2s run the Disruptive poach.

**Harder**

- The call comes while the disc is in the air.

**Easier**

- The call only comes on a stopped disc.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 24.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch.
drills.source: HN Bull Zone; HN Flik, Transitions

drills.title: Disruptive poach
drills.description:
