A planned poach off the pull: one defender plants in the open lane and the others cover.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (team defence) · Phase 2 (under pressure).

**How it runs**

1. Walk it: a defender plants in the open lane off the pull.
2. The others cover.
3. Then 7v7 from pulls with a planned poach.

**Coaching points**

- Everyone knows the plan.
- Flash the lane, then recover.
- Ask: "What did the poach make the offence do instead?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run the zone with a CRUMBLE call; they meet the planned poach in week 32.
- 2s: The 2s' toolkit block in week 24.

**Harder**

- The offence knows a poach is coming but not who.

**Easier**

- Name the poacher out loud before the pull.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 24.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch from a pull.

drills.title: Boxing out and finding the body
drills.description:
The 1v1 deep contest from both sides. It goes with theory Card 20.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Offence keeps their body between the disc and the defender.
2. Defence runs to the cutter and touches them first, then goes for the disc.
3. Three rounds: nobody jumps, offence jumps, both jump. Swap roles. Finish with deep running, the defender staying goal-side.

**Coaching points**

- Offence: body between. Defence: body first.
- Read the disc early and take the space in front.

**Harder**

- Both players jump from a running start.

**Easier**

- Nobody jumps.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 25.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes: thrower, cutter, defender; 30 m of space.
drills.source: GRUT (Amsterdam) deep drill videos; HN Practice Sessions 10; HB 27.4, 27.5

drills.title: Pulls in wind
drills.description:
Pulls in each wind direction before a windy event.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (set pieces) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Upwind: low, with extra IO. Downwind: keep it in. Then crosswind pulls.
2. Week 25: bladey and rolling pulls upwind and downwind.
3. Everyone else chases as a unit and calls "central" or "sideline".

**Coaching points**

- Pull straight back: a starter motor, not a discus.
- A pull that stays in is worth more than a long one that does not.
- Ask: "Which wind direction do you trust least?"

**Harder**

- Call your target third before each pull.
- Land in a 10 m target zone.

**Easier**

- Fewer pulls, full rest.
- Just land in bounds.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 25 and 30.
drills.setup_instructions: Pullers on the line; everyone else as the chase.

drills.title: Throwing in the wind
drills.description:
Low into it, high with it: throwing upwind and downwind in pairs.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Low release upwind.
2. High release downwind.
3. Extra spin on everything.

**Coaching points**

- Add spin until the disc stops wobbling.
- Keep it low and flat upwind.
- Ask: "Which way was harder, and what did you change?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Week 25: then the Bull zone refresh.
- 2s: Week 25: then the basic Bull zone walk-through.

**Harder**

- Across the wind, and at longer range.

**Easier**

- Closer together.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 25 and 30.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs, set up along the wind.

drills.title: Controller walk-through
drills.description:
Going through a zone: the controller gets every second pass, and a popper crashes the cup.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (zone offence) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Walk the controller: one handler gets every second pass.
2. A popper crashes the cup for a short pass.
3. If the crash is not thrown to, the popper gets out.

**Coaching points**

- Crash to reset the stall, gain yards or pull defenders in.
- Get out if you are not thrown to.
- Ask: "What did the crash do to the cup?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' drill in week 27.
- 2s: The 2s work on their top fix from Tour 1.

**Harder**

- A live cup.

**Easier**

- A cup that walks.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 27.
drills.setup_instructions: A bucket of handlers, a cup of three and a popper.
drills.source: Flik Zone Offence 2; HN Flik, Crashing the Cup

drills.title: Mini 3v3 with a controller
drills.description:
Zone offence through the middle as a small game: the controller must get every second pass.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (zone offence) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. 3v3.
2. One player is the controller and must get every second pass.
3. Swap the controller each point.

**Coaching points**

- Drive, then decide: if the middle is congested, dump and swing.
- Move as you throw.
- Ask: "When was going through the right choice, and when was around?"
- Ask: "What did the defenders do when the controller kept getting it back?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' game in week 27.
- 2s: The 2s play their top fix as a game.

**Harder**

- Stall 5.

**Easier**

- 3v2.
- One passive defender.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 27.
drills.setup_instructions: 3v3 on a small pitch.

drills.title: Endzone from 10 m
drills.description:
Converting from 10 m: vert stack, open-side cone, upfield dump.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (endzone) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Start 10 m out: vert stack, open-side cone, upfield dump.
2. Aim to score 3 out of 5.
3. Then scrimmage with a zone on every pull.

**Coaching points**

- Score before they recover.
- Reset patiently rather than forcing.
- Ask: "What did you do when the first cut was covered?"
- Ask: "Where did the poach come from, and who did it leave?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s also run "Spread".
- 2s: The 2s use the "Endzone" call only, with Last touch picks up in the scrimmage.

**Harder**

- Score 4 out of 5, or stall 6.
- 3 out of 3.
- 5 out of 5.

**Easier**

- 5v4.
- Start from 5 m.
- 3 out of 5.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 27.
drills.setup_instructions: An endzone and a line 10 m out.
drills.source: HB 26.4; Kieran; HN Flik, Endzone Offence

drills.title: Backhand and forehand huck technique
drills.description:
Huck technique built up in stages. It goes with theory Cards 10 and 11.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Backhand: sideways step, rotational load, pulled not pushed, slightly IO, arm extended at release.
2. Forehand: lateral, rotational and vertical loading; snap the arm back after release.
3. Build up: wrist only, then the step, then the full throw.

**Coaching points**

- Control, not power.
- Turn away, pull it through; stretch, turn, snap.
- Ask: "Where does the power come from?"

**Harder**

- Add a mark at stall 6.

**Easier**

- Stay at wrist-and-step until it is flat.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 28.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs with 40 m of space.
drills.source: GRUT (Amsterdam) huck videos; UAP Backhand hucks

drills.title: Box hucking
drills.description:
Hucks to a place, scored: land it in the box.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. A huck that lands in the box scores 1.
2. One the runner catches in stride in the box scores 2 (Herd's archery scoring).
3. Five hucks each, then rotate.

**Coaching points**

- Wind up to about 75% of your max range.
- Overthrown beats underthrown.
- Ask: "What did your misses have in common?"
- Ask: "What did the good ones have in common at release?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: Joint challenge with a runner (week 28).
- 2s: The 2s count hucks landing in the box, each thrower against their own last score.

**Harder**

- Move the box to the break side.

**Easier**

- A bigger box, closer in.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 28.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes: thrower, runner, retriever. A 10 x 10 m box at about 75% of the thrower's range.
drills.source: HN Practice Sessions 9; HN Excel Premium; UAP Backhand hucks

drills.title: Deep running drill
drills.description:
Deep running with the defender staying goal-side, then with an in-cut option.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. The runner goes deep; the defender stays goal-side.
2. Week 28: add an in-cut option after 20-25 m.
3. First two reps at 80%. One sprint cue per rep: lean forward, pull the rope, look at the horizon.

**Coaching points**

- Sprint, then look sideways at the disc.
- Cut through the middle, not along the sideline.
- Ask: "When did you look for the disc?"

**Harder**

- The thrower chooses deep or in-cut late.
- The defender starts level.

**Easier**

- No defender.
- A 2 m head start.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 28.
drills.setup_instructions: Thrower, runner and defender; 40 m of space.

drills.title: Move the Mark
drills.description:
Hucking past a mark, built up by effort.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Huck against a stationary mark at 50%.
2. Then 70%.
3. Then 100%.

**Coaching points**

- Pump-fake one side and huck the other.
- Set it up first: power position or straight after a swing.
- Ask: "What did the mark take away, and what did you use instead?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' throwing block in week 28.
- 2s: The 2s run Box hucking.

**Harder**

- A live mark.

**Easier**

- Stay at 70%.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 28.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes: thrower, mark, receiver.
drills.source: HN Excel Premium; UAP Backhand hucks

drills.title: Dishy Huck
drills.description:
The huck from power position: a dish to a handler moving upfield, then the deep shot. Deep-cut timing for the cutter.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. 3v3: handler, dish and deep cutter against three defenders.
2. A huck caught in stride scores 2.
3. A stop scores 1 for the defence.

**Coaching points**

- Go deep when the thrower is in power position.
- Start shallow so the space stays open.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' game in week 28.
- 2s: The 2s run Deep cut timing with a dish.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 28.
drills.setup_instructions: 3v3: handler, dish and deep cutter against three defenders.

drills.title: Deep cut timing with a dish
drills.description:
The 2s' version of Dishy Huck: when to go deep.

**Serves:** Getting open · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. The handler takes a dish and is in power position.
2. The deep cutter waits for it, starting shallow.
3. Then they are decisive: go.

**Coaching points**

- Wait for the trigger.
- Shallow, wait, go.
- Ask: "What told you it was time to go?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play Dishy Huck, 3v3.
- 2s: The 2s' drill in week 28.

**Harder**

- Add a deep defender.

**Easier**

- The thrower calls "go".

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 28.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes: handler, dish and deep cutter.

drills.title: Ho deep shots
drills.description:
Deep shots from the ho: isolate a cutter and run diagonal scoring cuts.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Walk it: isolate a cutter.
2. Run diagonal scoring cuts from the open side to the break-side back corner.
3. Then 7v7 in ho.

**Coaching points**

- Huck after a swing, before the mark sets.
- Lead it slightly to the break side.
- Ask: "Who was isolated, and who cleared for them?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' toolkit block in week 28.
- 2s: The 2s run Back of stack goes deep from vert.

**Harder**

- The defence may put a deep help defender in.

**Easier**

- Walk it, then 5v5.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 28.

drills.source: HN Deep Dives, Italy Mixed WUC 2024

drills.title: Back of stack goes deep from vert
drills.description:
The 2s' deep shot: the back of the vert stack goes deep.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Walk it: the back of the stack goes deep on the trigger.
2. Then 7v7 in vert, with Three new handlers.

**Coaching points**

- Go when the door opens: power position, an upline cut, or after a swing.
- Sprint, then look sideways.
- Ask: "What was the trigger?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run Ho deep shots.
- 2s: The 2s' toolkit block in week 28.

**Harder**

- A deep defender starts 5 m off.

**Easier**

- Walk it, then 5v5.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 28.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch in a vertical stack.

drills.title: Line-trap game
drills.description:
The arrowhead's line trap as a game: both teams play a zone with a chase and two tips, adding a sideline trap.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (zones) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. 7v7: both teams play a zone with a chase and two tips in the lanes.
2. Add the sideline trap once the disc reaches the line.

**Coaching points**

- Wall up, do not get outflanked.
- Once the disc is on the line, close it.
- Ask: "Who closed the trap, and what throw was left?"
- Ask: "When did you have to get off the line by?"

**Harder**

- The offence may go over the top.
- Stall 6.

**Easier**

- The offence may only swing and crash.
- Offence 7v6.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 30.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch.

drills.title: Upwind-downwind game
drills.description:
Playing the wind: an upwind goal is worth three downwind ones.

**Serves:** Seeing the field · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. 5v5 along the wind.
2. An upwind goal scores 3.
3. A downwind goal scores 1.

**Coaching points**

- Bigger spaces, fewer throws.
- Get the disc off the downwind sideline.
- Ask: "What did you change going upwind?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run the arrowhead and the wind plan.
- 2s: The 2s' game in week 30.

**Harder**

- Stall 6 upwind.

**Easier**

- 5v4 going upwind.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 30.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v5 on a pitch set along the wind.

drills.title: Safe vert in wind
drills.description:
The 2s' wind offence: a short stack, big under cuts and backing each other up.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Walk it: a short stack.
2. Big under cuts.
3. Back up every throw.

**Coaching points**

- Low into it, high with it.
- Get bodies under every disc.
- Ask: "Who was backing up that throw?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s build the wind plan around the arrowhead.
- 2s: The 2s' toolkit block in week 30.

**Harder**

- Run it live as a wind scrimmage in vert.

**Easier**

- Walk it downwind first.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 30.

drills.source: Flik Zone Concepts 6; HN Deep Dives

drills.title: Pulling game
drills.description:
Pulls with a score, so pullers can track them.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (set pieces) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Each puller throws nine pulls.
2. Each is scored 0-4: in bounds, right shape, target third, in the endzone.
3. Everyone else practises the chase.

**Coaching points**

- Pick a target before you start.
- Little and often, including when you are tired.
- Ask: "What did your best pull have that the others did not?"

**Harder**

- Into the wind.

**Easier**

- Six pulls and a bigger target.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 31.
drills.setup_instructions: Pullers on the line; the pitch marked in thirds.

drills.title: Pull chase and first-pass defence
drills.description:
Both ends of the pull: the defence chases as a unit and the offence fields it.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (set pieces) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. The defence chases as a unit and calls "central" or "sideline".
2. The offence fields as "1" and "2".
3. Play out the first pass.

**Coaching points**

- Everyone knows the coverage.
- Chasers call early.
- Ask: "Was the defence set before the disc was centred?"

**Harder**

- Play on to three passes.

**Easier**

- Walk the coverage first.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 31.
drills.setup_instructions: A pulling line of seven and a receiving "1" and "2".
drills.source: HN Handler Situations; Flik Zone Concepts 6

drills.title: Throw-and-go pairs
drills.description:
Throwing in pairs with three fast steps after every throw: towards, left, right, away.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Throw to your partner.
2. Take three fast steps: towards, left, right or away.
3. Change direction each throw.

**Coaching points**

- Start running as the disc leaves your hand.
- If your pivot foot moves before the release, slow down.
- Ask: "Which direction was hardest to throw and go?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run Quick throwing.
- 2s: The 2s' throwing block in week 32.

**Harder**

- The partner returns the disc on the move.

**Easier**

- Two steps at jog pace.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 32.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs, 10 m apart.

drills.title: 3v3 possession
drills.description:
Keeping the disc as a three: ten passes for a point, and the disc has to keep finding new players.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. 3v3 in a square.
2. 10 passes scores a point.
3. Every third throw must go to a new player.

**Coaching points**

- Move as you throw.
- Seal the lane after an open-side throw.
- Ask: "How did you get free for the return pass?"
- Ask: "What did you do straight after you threw?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play Dominator 3v3 with a poacher.
- 2s: The 2s' game in week 32.

**Harder**

- Stall 5.

**Easier**

- 3v2.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 32.
drills.setup_instructions: 3v3 in a 20 x 20 m square.

drills.title: Box give-and-go
drills.description:
Give-and-go movement: there is always a free cone to move to.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Three players, four cones.
2. After every throw, move to the free cone.
3. Keep the disc moving.

**Coaching points**

- Throw and go.
- Throw the dish to the gut; no need to lead it.
- Ask: "Where was the free cone, and who saw it first?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run the Dominator drill with a poaching defender.
- 2s: The 2s' drill in week 32.

**Harder**

- Add a defender in the middle.

**Easier**

- Walk it first.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 32.
drills.setup_instructions: Three players and four cones in a square.

drills.title: Two-on-two with switching
drills.description:
The basic switch: two cutters cross and the defenders call it and swap.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (team defence) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Two cutters, two defenders.
2. The cutters cross.
3. The defenders call and switch.

**Coaching points**

- Early, loud, by name.
- Never switch onto a cutter already at full speed away from you.
- Ask: "Who called it, and was it early enough?"

**Harder**

- The cutters may fake the cross.
- The cutters decide when to cross.

**Easier**

- Walk the cross and call it.
- They cross on a whistle.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 33.
drills.setup_instructions: Two cutters, two defenders, a thrower.

drills.title: Random calls
drills.description:
Reacting to a call mid-rep: the coach calls "switch", "poach" or "stay".

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (team defence) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Run a 2v2 rep.
2. The coach calls "switch", "poach" or "stay" mid-rep.
3. Defenders react immediately.

**Coaching points**

- The caller decides.
- After a switch, new matchups hold until the next stoppage.
- Ask: "What did you do in the first second after the call?"

**Harder**

- A teammate calls instead of the coach.
- A call every 2 seconds.

**Easier**

- The call comes before the rep starts.
- One call per rep.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 33.
drills.setup_instructions: Two cutters, two defenders, a thrower; a coach calling.

drills.title: Bull zone: the bull's role in pairs
drills.description:
The bull's job in isolation: force the throw high.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (zones) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. One thrower, one bull, two targets.
2. The bull forces the throw high.
3. Rotate after five throws.

**Coaching points**

- The bull makes the throw ugly; the block comes from someone else.
- Sit just behind the chases, not close enough to double-team.
- Ask: "Where did the ugly throw go?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' throwing block in week 33.
- 2s: The 2s run Poaching footwork in pairs.

**Harder**

- The thrower may fake.

**Easier**

- The targets stand closer together.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 33.
drills.setup_instructions: One thrower, one bull, two targets.

drills.title: Zone blocks
drills.description:
Getting blocks out of the Bull zone in congested spaces.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (zones) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Walk through where the blocks come from: the wings and the middle reading the forced throw.
2. 8-pull: the defence scores 2 for a block by a wing or the middle on a forced throw.
3. Any other turnover scores 1.

**Coaching points**

- Zone is not half effort.
- Count the attackers in your area every time the disc moves.
- Ask: "Who got the block, and who forced the throw?"
- Ask: "Which throw were we forcing? Who was reading it?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' toolkit block in week 33.
- 2s: The 2s run Poaching as a team.

**Harder**

- The offence may go over the top.

**Easier**

- The offence may only swing and crash.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 33.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch; the defence pulls eight times (8-pull).

drills.title: Poaching footwork in pairs
drills.description:
The footwork of a poach: leave, then get back.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (team defence) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Poach into the lane.
2. Recover to your player.
3. A recovery that beats the throw scores a point.

**Coaching points**

- Flash the lane: leave just long enough to deny one throw.
- Three compact steps beat a panicked chase.
- Ask: "How long could you stay in the lane and still get back?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s work on the bull's role.
- 2s: The 2s' throwing block in week 33.

**Harder**

- The thrower may fake the throw to your player.

**Easier**

- A slower count before the throw.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 33.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs with a thrower: one attacker, one defender.

drills.title: Poaching as a team
drills.description:
What everyone else does when one defender poaches.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (team defence) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Walk it: one person poaches.
2. Everyone shifts.
3. Reset and repeat from a new disc position.

**Coaching points**

- If one person poaches, everyone shifts.
- Pick up the next player as soon as you leave the last.
- Ask: "Who was left free, and who took them?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s run Zone blocks.
- 2s: The 2s' drill in week 33.

**Harder**

- Run it live in 7v6.

**Easier**

- Freeze after each pass.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 33.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch.

drills.title: Minimum-time game
drills.description:
Patience: no score before 90 seconds of possession. The partner of the Shot clock game.

**Serves:** Seeing the field · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Play 5v5.
2. No score counts before 90 seconds of possession.
3. Anything earlier does not count.

**Coaching points**

- It is never a bad idea to use the dump.
- Every touch has a job; if it has none and is not safe, hold it and dump.
- Ask: "What did you do differently when you could not score yet?"
- Ask: "How did you keep the disc without going backwards?"

**Harder**

- Two minutes, or stall 6.
- 120 seconds at stall 6.

**Easier**

- 60 seconds, or 5v4.
- 60 seconds.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 34.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v5 on a 35 x 25 m pitch with endzones.
drills.source: Ian French, Games for Coaching Ultimate Frisbee

drills.title: Throwing over the cup
drills.description:
Going over a zone on purpose: hammers and blades over a cup.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (zone offence) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. One thrower, a cup of three, a target behind.
2. Throw over the cup to the target.
3. Rotate.

**Coaching points**

- Only throw it when the target is open behind the cup and you have a clean release.
- Blades and scoobers get over quicker; hammers go further.
- Ask: "What made that one safe to throw?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' throwing block in week 34.
- 2s: The 2s run the 3H shape walk-through.

**Harder**

- Add a wing behind the cup.
- An active cup.

**Easier**

- A cup of two.
- A static cup.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 34.
drills.setup_instructions: One thrower, a cup of three, a target behind.

drills.title: Deep cutters drag the deep defenders
drills.description:
Opening the middle for the over-the-top throw: deep cutters drag the deeps back.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (zone offence) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Deep cutters drag the deep defenders back.
2. The middle space opens for the over-the-top throw.
3. Walked, then at pace.

**Coaching points**

- Go over on purpose, not in hope.
- It must not float into a wing.
- Ask: "What opened when the deeps went back?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' toolkit block in week 34.
- 2s: The 2s run 3H against person D.

**Harder**

- Run it as an 8-pull against the Bull zone.

**Easier**

- Walk it with the zone frozen.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 34.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch against a zone.

drills.title: Zone offence over the top
drills.description:
The third way to beat a zone, in reps: over the top against the Bull zone.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (zone offence) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. The offence receives eight pulls against the Bull zone.
2. Look for the over-the-top throw when the deeps are dragged back.
3. If it is not on, go around or through.

**Coaching points**

- Swing it, crash it, or go over it.
- Only throw the hammer when the target is open behind the cup.
- Ask: "Which of the three ways did the zone give you?"
- Ask: "Was that planned, or desperate?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' game in week 34.
- 2s: The 2s keep to around and through.

**Harder**

- Add a shot clock.

**Easier**

- The wings start a step deeper.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 34.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch; the offence receives eight pulls (8-pull) against the Bull zone.
drills.source: Flik Zone Offence 9; Flik Upfield Dump

drills.title: 3H shape walk-through
drills.description:
The 2s meet vert from the front: three handlers at the back, and the front of the stack as an upfield reset.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Walk the shape: three handlers at the back.
2. The front of the stack is an upfield reset.
3. Cuts go away from the disc or across the pitch.

**Coaching points**

- A lateral throw to the 3H gains yards and opens the break side.
- The first cut has to be real.
- Ask: "Where is the 3H when the disc is on the sideline?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s have run this since week 6.
- 2s: The 2s' throwing block in week 34.

**Harder**

- Add defenders on the handlers.

**Easier**

- Use cones for each position.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 34.
drills.setup_instructions: A vertical stack with three handlers.

drills.title: 3H against person D
drills.description:
Vert from the front as a game for the 2s: only certain cuts may be thrown to.

**Serves:** The offence toolkit (structures) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. 5v5 in the 3H shape against person defence.
2. Only cuts away from the disc or across the pitch may be thrown to.
3. Then 7v7 with live defence on the handlers.

**Coaching points**

- Offset lateral cuts into the undefended channel.
- Cut in the lane, recover in the stack.
- Ask: "Which cut was open most often?"
- Ask: "Where did the space open when the cutters went away?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s play zone offence over the top.
- 2s: The 2s' game in week 34.

**Harder**

- 7v7 with live defence on the handlers.
- Live defence on the handlers.

**Easier**

- 5v4.
- Half pace.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 34.
drills.setup_instructions: 5v5, then 7v7, in a vertical stack with three handlers.

drills.title: 1s v 2s with handicaps
drills.description:
A fair game between the squads: handicaps make both sides work on something.

**Serves:** Seeing the field · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. The 1s play the 2s on a full pitch.
2. For example: the 1s play stall 7 and must complete one break throw before scoring.
3. The 2s start points with the disc.

**Coaching points**

- Use a different way to get open on each point (Card 16).
- Judge the game on process goals, not the score.
- Ask: "Which handicap changed how you played?"

**Harder**

- Tighten the 1s' handicap if they lead by three.

**Easier**

- Loosen it if the 2s lead by three.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 35.
drills.setup_instructions: A full pitch; the 1s against the 2s.

drills.title: Your three throws for your role
drills.description:
Each player's throwing progression for their role, at game speed, in mentor pairs.

**Serves:** The throwing and catching base · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Name the three throws your role uses most.
2. Throw them at game speed with your mentor pair.
3. Swap after ten of each.

**Coaching points**

- Hands before legs: quick release at game speed.
- Throw the ones your game plan needs, not your favourites.
- Ask: "Which of your three is least reliable at game speed?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s' throwing block in week 36.
- 2s: The 2s run Get 10 as a race between threes.

**Harder**

- Add a mark at stall 5.

**Easier**

- Two throws instead of three.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 36.
drills.setup_instructions: Mentor pairs.
drills.source: Season plan, Throwing outside training; Flik L4 Lesson 1

drills.title: "What if" scrimmage
drills.description:
Game management under pressure: the coach changes the score or the conditions mid-game.

**Serves:** Seeing the field · Phases 3-4 (in the team) and Phase 5 (Nationals: nothing new).

**How it runs**

1. Play 7v7.
2. The coach changes the score or conditions mid-game, for example "you're two breaks down, go".
3. Teams use their reset routine.

**Coaching points**

- Know the risk and reward of the score and the clock.
- One breath, one cue word, next job.
- Ask: "What changed in your decisions when the score changed?"
- Ask: "What did we say we'd do when this happened? Did we do it?"
- Ask: "What was your cue word? Did it bring you back to the next job?"

**Harder**

- Add a timeout the captains must use.
- Change the conditions twice a game.

**Easier**

- One change per game, announced at a stoppage.
- Once a game.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 36, 41 and 47.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch.
drills.source: HN Coach Corner, Preparing for Pressure

drills.title: 3v3 scoring game
drills.description:
Taking away the open side: the offence is paid for open-side catches, so the defence has to stop them.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. 3v3 with a one-way force.
2. The offence gets 2 points for each open-side catch.
3. The defence gets 1 point for each block, so it has to block the open side.

**Coaching points**

- Take away the first option, every time.
- A mark that forces hard makes every other defender's job easier.
- Ask: "What did the defence have to give up to stop the open side?"

**Harder**

- Stall 5.
- A smaller pitch.

**Easier**

- A spare defender.
- A bigger pitch.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 38.
drills.setup_instructions: 3v3 on a small pitch with a one-way force.

drills.title: Mark-call drill
drills.description:
Switching marks on a call: the drill version of the Mark-call game.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (marking and 1v1 defence) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Thrower against mark.
2. The coach calls "triangle" or "flat" mid-stall.
3. The mark changes at once.

**Coaching points**

- Know the thrower, pick the mark.
- On the call, everyone downfield knows the open side has changed.
- Ask: "What did the thrower get in the second before you changed?"

**Harder**

- Add a receiver and a live throw.
- The call comes at stall 2.

**Easier**

- The call comes before the stall starts.
- The call comes before the stall.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 39.
drills.setup_instructions: Pairs: thrower and mark; a coach calling.

drills.title: Line trap in fours
drills.description:
The arrowhead's line trap in a small group: the chase and two tips close the line on a thrower and a reset.

**Serves:** The defence toolkit (zones) · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. A thrower and a reset on the sideline.
2. The chase and two tips close the line.
3. Rotate roles.

**Coaching points**

- Trap it on the line: take away the escape throws.
- Wall up, do not get outflanked.
- Ask: "Which escape throw was left open?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: The 1s have had the line trap since week 30.
- 2s: The 2s' drill in week 39, as they take on the arrowhead in full.

**Harder**

- The reset may cut upline.

**Easier**

- The thrower may not fake.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 39.
drills.setup_instructions: Fives on a sideline: a thrower and a reset against a chase and two tips. In fours, play with one tip.

drills.title: Retention game
drills.description:
Only throw to players who are free: a throw to a covered player costs a point even if it is caught.

**Serves:** Keeping the disc · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Play 7v7.
2. A throw to a player who was not open scores a point for the defence, even if it is caught.
3. A goal without a turnover scores 2.

**Coaching points**

- Free means separation, the right hips and a lane.
- Right option first, then the right throw.
- Ask: "Was that the right option? Was the throw good?"
- Ask: "Was the receiver open, or just close?"

**Harder**

- Stall 6.

**Easier**

- 7v6.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 40.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch.

drills.title: Escape game
drills.description:
Escaping what the opposition will do: the defence plays the looks from the scouting cards.

**Serves:** Seeing the field · Phases 3-4 (in the team).

**How it runs**

1. Play 7v7.
2. The defence plays the looks from the scouting cards: poaches, junk, a zone.
3. The offence scores double for a score without a turnover.

**Coaching points**

- Train how to escape the situation, not just how to recognise it.
- Obvious beats clever.
- Ask: "What told you which look they were in?"
- Ask: "What was the look? What was our answer on the scouting card?"

**Harder**

- The defence changes look mid-point.

**Easier**

- The defence says which look it is in.
- The defence announces its look.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** week 40.
drills.setup_instructions: 7v7 on a full pitch.

drills.title: Mini-test
drills.description:
Two of the four skill tests in 20 minutes, every 4-6 weeks, so every player sees their curve between the full test rounds.

**Serves:** Measuring improvement · Phase 1 (technique), Phase 2 (under pressure), Phases 3-4 (in the team) and Phase 5 (Nationals: nothing new).

**How it runs**

1. Get 10: 10 throws past a marker to a static receiver 10-15 m away, against each force.
2. The 1v1 cutting test: 10 reps from a stack spot 15 m out against a back-shoulder defender, until stall 6.
3. Players log their own scores in the home programme's Tests.

**Coaching points**

- The point is each player's curve, not today's number.
- Use the same set-up every time; the full protocols are at the top of the Phase 1 sessions tab.

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: 1s defenders play at full intensity in the cutting test.
- 2s: Same test and same scoring: difficulty does not change, so the scores can be compared.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 6, 10, 15, 22, 27, 32, 40 and 45.
drills.setup_instructions: Threes for Get 10; fours for the 1v1 cutting test (thrower, cutter, defender, counter).

drills.title: Skill test stations
drills.description:
A full round of the skill tests run as stations: Trial 1 (week 18), mid-season (week 35) and the final round (week 51). October's round is the Baseline tests.

**Serves:** Measuring improvement · Phase 2 (under pressure), Phases 3-4 (in the team) and Phase 5 (Nationals: nothing new).

**How it runs**

1. Five stations of 12 minutes; everyone does all five.
2. The four skill tests: hucking alley, Get 10 (both forces), the 1v1 cutting test, heads-on catching.
3. Plus the filmed 5-10-5. At Trial 1 the 50 m sprint and the arrowhead agility test are added.

**Coaching points**

- Keep it quick and positive.
- Players enter their own results and agree one development focus afterwards.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 18, 35 and 51.
drills.setup_instructions: Five stations of 12 minutes with 5 minutes for changeovers; groups of 8-10.
drills.equipment_needed: discs, cones, a phone for filming, printed test sheet

drills.title: Skill floor
drills.description:
Protected time for individual work in every full joint session from week 25: 25 minutes straight after the warm-up, in self-running groups of three.

**Serves:** Measuring improvement · Phases 3-4 (in the team) and Phase 5 (Nationals: nothing new).

**How it runs**

1. 12 minutes on one partner's development focus, then 12 on the other's; the third player defends or marks.
2. Roles rotate after every rep, so nobody waits more than one rep.
3. Pick the activity for the focus: getting open (1v1 "name your cut", 1v1 from the stack spot), breaking the mark (Extended mark, One-crossover marking game, Get 10), catching and hucking (Turn and attack, Box hucking, Read-the-defender hucking), marking and 1v1 defence (Triangle marking progression, Win the Box, Keeping margins).

**Coaching points**

- Skill leads move between lanes and fix one thing per group.
- Players write their score in their log.
- Ask: "What is your development focus, and what did you score today?"

**1s and 2s**

- 1s: 1s players work side by side with their mentor partner.
- 2s: The same activities and scoring; the mentor chooses the starting difficulty.

**Harder**

- Use each activity's harder option when a group scores 8 out of 10.

**Easier**

- Use the easier option when a group scores under 4 out of 10.

**In the 2027/28 plan:** weeks 25, 28, 30, 33, 34, 36, 38, 39 and 46.
drills.setup_instructions: Groups of three, one lane each, a disc per group (two for the extended mark). Each group is a mentor pair plus one more.
